description: The convoy of the locomotive 15 operated by Mr. Tito is located in hopper OP2 positioning the 1st car under the hopper, the assistant does not observe anything out of the ordinary (dry load there is no presence of water) and initiates the chute, for this, the hydraulic module of the hopper is switched on and with the controls it slightly moves the hopper handle and an untimely flow of water and mud splashes the operator generating the described injury, in addition the collaborator was 7 meters from the line of fire

This is the same underlying mechanism as "mud rushes" or "uncontrolled draw point releases," which are recognized in the mining industry as capable of causing serious injury, entrapment, or fatality due to the force, volume, and speed of material release. Critically, the operator was struck by the splash from 7 meters away, which indicates the release carried significant energy/force — not a gentle drip or seep. The explicit mention that the collaborator was in the "line of fire" at that distance reinforces that this was a hazard zone with a genuine escalation pathway, and the actual outcome (a splash injury) reflects a fortunate variation of an event that could plausibly have been far more severe (e.g., higher volume/pressure release, closer proximity, or being caught in the flow path).
